title: The Musgrave Ritual
summary: Holmes investigates a strange family paper that leads him to a hidden secret.
coverScene: A tall man in a dark coat stands under a large oak tree at dusk, holding an old rolled paper while a small dog watches nearby.

sentences.text: Long ago, my friend Holmes told me a story.
It was not his normal work.
A man came to see Holmes one night.
His name was Reginald Musgrave.
He looked worried and needed help.
Musgrave told Holmes about his family’s old rule.
For many years, the oldest son had to do something.
He had to answer some questions.
This was called the Musgrave Rule.
It was on a piece of paper.
The questions were always the same.
No one knew what they really meant.
Musgrave said, 'I never thought about it before.'
He told Holmes his worker, Brunton, was gone.
Before he left, Brunton acted in a different way.
He read the Rule late at night.
He asked about old family history.
Musgrave saw him look at the paper.
He told Brunton to leave the house.
Brunton asked to stay a few more days.
The next morning, Brunton was not there.
His bed was not used.
His things were still in his room.
Musgrave looked but found nothing.
Then a woman named Rachel Howells felt bad.
She was close to Brunton.
She did not want to see him again.
Holmes listened and asked to see the Rule.
The paper said: 'Whose was it? His who is gone.'
It also said: 'Who shall have it? He who will come.'
It talked about a tree and a place.
Holmes thought for a moment.
He said, 'This is not just a rule—it shows a place.'
He decided to go to Musgrave’s house.
When they got there, Holmes looked at an old tree.
He measured its shade to find a place on the ground.
Then he asked about the house’s history.
He learned part of the house was very old.
Holmes said, 'The answer is under the old part.'
They went to a room below the house.
It was dark and not clean.
They found a small box under some rocks.
Inside was an old thing for the head.
It was for a leader long ago.
Holmes said the Rule kept the thing safe.
The questions helped find it.
Only the oldest son could understand them.
Brunton knew the answer and wanted the thing.
Holmes then found Brunton’s body.
Brunton went to take the thing.
He got stuck when the door closed.
Rachel Howells knew what happened.
She felt so bad that she left.
The problem was over.
It was a bad end for Brunton.
Musgrave was happy to have the thing back.
But he felt sorry for what happened.
Holmes said some family rules hide more than words.
They can hide things that are better not found.
The Musgrave Rule was one of those things.
It led to a bad end.
After that day, Musgrave kept the thing in a better place.
Holmes never forgot how simple questions could change lives.

He looked worried and said he needed help.
Musgrave told Holmes about his family’s old custom.

This was called the Musgrave Ritual.
It was written on a piece of paper.

No one knew what they meant.
Musgrave said, 'I never thought about it much before now.'
He told Holmes that a man who worked for him, Brunton, had left.
Before he left, Brunton acted in a strange way.
Musgrave saw him reading the Ritual late at night.
Brunton also asked questions about old family history.
Musgrave found him looking at the paper and got angry.
He told Brunton to leave the house.
Brunton asked to stay for a few more days.
Musgrave said yes.
The next morning, Brunton was gone.
His bed had not been slept in.
His things were still in his room.
Musgrave looked everywhere but found nothing.
Then, a woman named Rachel Howells became very ill.
She had been close to Brunton.
She cried all the time and said she never wanted to see him again.
Holmes listened and asked to see the Ritual.
The paper had these words: 'Whose was it? His who is gone.'
'Who shall have it? He who will come.'
It also talked about a tree and a place where something was hidden.
Holmes thought for a moment.
He said, 'This is not just a custom—it is like a map.'
He decided to go to Musgrave’s house right away.
When they arrived, Holmes looked at the big tree.
It was very tall.
He measured the ground near it to find a special spot.
Then he asked Musgrave about the house’s past.
Holmes learned that part of the house was very old.
He said, 'The answer must be under the old part of the house.'
They went to a room below the house.
It was dark and had not been used for a long time.
In that room, they found a small, heavy box under some stones.
Inside was an old gold thing that had belonged to a king long ago.
Holmes explained that the Ritual was a way to keep the gold thing safe.
The questions helped find it.
Only the family’s oldest son could understand them.
Brunton had figured it out and wanted the gold thing for himself.
Then Holmes found Brunton’s body in a small room near the old part.
He had gone there to take the gold thing.
The door closed and he could not get out.
Rachel Howells knew what happened.
She felt so bad that she ran away.
The event was solved, but it was a sad end for Brunton.
Musgrave was glad to have the gold thing back.
But he also felt sorry.

They can hide things that are better left alone.
The Musgrave Ritual was one of those things.

He often thought about it when he worked on other cases.

Musgrave learned that the hard way.
He told his son about the Ritual when he was older.
He wanted to make sure the same thing would not happen again.
The son promised to be careful with the family’s past.
Holmes and I talked about the case many times after that.
We agreed that some things are better left hidden.
The gold thing stayed safe, but the memory of Brunton did not.
Musgrave never forgot the man who tried to take what was not his.
He also never forgot the woman who ran away because of it.
The house stayed quiet after that.
No one talked about the Ritual much.
But everyone knew it was still there, waiting.
Waiting for the next person who might try to solve it.

sentences.text: Many years ago, my friend Sherlock Holmes told me about a strange event he worked on.
It was not like his usual cases.
It began with an old family trouble.
A man called Reginald Musgrave came to see Holmes one evening in London.
Musgrave looked troubled and said he needed help with something very important.
He explained his family had a special rule.
For hundreds of years, every oldest son in the family had to answer a set of questions.
This was called the Musgrave Custom, and it was written on paper.
The questions were always the same, but no one knew what they truly meant.
Musgrave said, 'I never gave it much thought until now.'
He told Holmes that a man who worked for him, named Brunton, had left.
Before he left, Brunton had acted in a strange way.
He was seen reading the Custom late at night and asking about old family history.
Musgrave caught him looking at the paper and became angry.
He told Brunton to leave the house, but Brunton asked to stay for a few more days.
The next morning, Brunton was gone.
His bed had not been slept in, and his things were still in his room.
Musgrave searched everywhere in the house and garden but found nothing.
Then, a woman who worked for him, named Rachel Howells, became very upset.
She had been close to Brunton and cried all the time.
She said she never wanted to see him again.
Holmes listened carefully and asked to see the Custom.
The paper had these words: 'Whose was it? His who is gone.', 'Who shall have it? He who will come.'
It also spoke of a tree and a place where something was kept.
Holmes thought for a moment and said, 'This is not just a rule—it is like a guide.'
He decided to go to Musgrave’s house at once to solve the trouble.
When they arrived, Holmes looked at the tall tree mentioned in the Custom.
He measured its shadow to find a special spot on the ground.
Then he asked Musgrave about the history of the house.
He learned that part of it was very old.
Holmes said, 'The answer must be under the old part of the house.'
They went to a dark room below the house that was full of dust.
In that room, they found a small, heavy box hidden under some stones.
Inside was an old gold circle that had belonged to a king long ago.
Holmes explained that the Custom was a way to keep it safe.
The questions were like signs to find it, and only the family’s oldest son could understand them.
Brunton had figured it out and wanted it for himself.
Holmes then found Brunton’s body in a small room near the dark room below.
He had gone there to take the gold circle but got trapped when the door closed behind him.
Rachel Howells knew what had happened and was so upset that she ran away.
The trouble was solved, but it was a bad end for Brunton.
Musgrave was glad to have the gold circle back but felt sorry for what had happened.
Holmes told me that some family rules hold more than just words.
They can hide secrets that might be better if they stayed hidden.
The Musgrave Custom was one of those secrets, and it led to a very bad end.
From that day on, Musgrave kept the gold circle in a safer place.

It was a lesson he never forgot.

If he had, perhaps Brunton would not have tried to take the gold circle.

We both agreed that some things are better left unknown.

It was a secret that brought only sorrow and loss.
Many years have passed since that case, but I still remember it clearly.
It was one of the most unusual events Holmes ever worked on.
The Custom seemed simple, but it held a dangerous secret.
No one in the family had realized how much trouble it could cause.
Brunton’s curiosity led him to discover the gold circle’s hiding place.
He thought he could take it without anyone knowing.
But the room where it was hidden was old and dangerous.
The door closed behind him, and he could not get out.
Rachel Howells knew what had happened but was too upset to speak.
She ran away and was never seen again.

He wished he had paid more attention to the Custom earlier.

The gold circle was now safe, but the cost had been very high.

Holmes and I often wondered what would have happened if Brunton had not been so curious.
Perhaps he would still be alive, and Rachel would not have run away.
But some people cannot resist the chance to find something valuable.
Brunton was one of those people, and it cost him his life.

It was only when Brunton tried to solve it that the trouble began.
